judge_assessment.explanation: The judge's value claims check out: the sticker strip holds 6 stars and 8 moons so the ratio is 3/4 and the part-to-whole is 6/14 = 3/7; the tape diagram's 7 boxes at 6 beads give 42; the bead table scales to 2 and 10; 84 bottles in 4 minutes is 21 per minute; fiction is 3/8 of the shelf; the ticket table gives 4 and 20; 3/5 < 5/8; the lemonade table gives 3 and 45; and 63 litres split 5:4 gives 35 litres of blue. Tape diagrams and tables do connect words, colon notation and fractions as the judge says. Two things contradict the perfect score. First, four problems require a written or drawn response and none is declared manual: problem 2 ('say in words what that fraction tells you about the sheet'), problem 4 ('Say which way you scaled to reach each one'), problem 6 ('Explain where the denominator of your fraction comes from, since it is not one of the two numbers in the ratio'), and problem 10 ('Draw a tape diagram with one box per share'). verify.json has no manual entry and gate_log.txt reports '13 passed, 0 failed, 0 manual'. Second, two problems print more requested responses than are verified: problem 1 asks for the ratio 'in all three forms' and then in simplest form, and only the simplified 3/4 is checked; problem 8 asks for each mix as a fraction and the value of each ratio before the relation, and only the relation is checked. The Quick Answers bank also prints '8. ---' because the relation fails to sympify.

strengths_to_preserve: Problem 3's tape diagram carries no numbers on the boxes - the stem supplies 'Each box holds 6 beads' - so the student must count all seven boxes rather than read a total off the picture, and the declared trap (24, from counting only the red boxes) is exactly the error that design invites.
The three written forms are stated once at the top with the ordering rule that actually causes errors: 'the quantity named first in the question is written first'.

Problems 4, 7 and 9 are three ratio tables at rising difficulty where the missing cells force different scaling directions, and problem 9's stem coaches the order of operations on the table itself ('Fill in the middle column first - dividing is the easy step - then use that column to reach 30 cups').

root_causes.description: Items that require a written diagnosis or a drawn representation are recorded as machine verified because a numeric companion value exists, so the gate log reports zero manual items for a sheet full of open responses. The manual type exists and is used correctly on other cases in this same run, which shows the contract is author discretion rather than an enforced rule.
evidence: evals/runs/curriculum-shardX-20260802T194403Z/tasks/curr-151/worksheet.pdf problem 2 ('say in words what that fraction tells you'), problem 4 ('Say which way you scaled to reach each one'), problem 6 ('Explain where the denominator ... comes from'), problem 10 ('Draw a tape diagram with one box per share')
evals/runs/curriculum-shardX-20260802T194403Z/tasks/curr-151/verify.json contains no 'manual' entry; all thirteen entries are eval, solve or compare

root_causes.description: The verify JSON is authored one entry per problem id rather than one entry per printed response, so a stem that asks for two things is recorded as fully machine verified when only its last component was checked. Nothing in the gate chain compares the number of answer locations the sheet prints against the number of entries covering them.
evidence: evals/runs/curriculum-shardX-20260802T194403Z/tasks/curr-151/worksheet.pdf problem 1: 'Write the ratio of star stickers to moon stickers in all three forms, then give that ratio in simplest form as a fraction' - four requested responses, one verify entry (expected '3/4')

evals/runs/curriculum-shardX-20260802T194403Z/tasks/curr-151/worksheet.pdf problem 8: 'Write each mix as a ratio in fraction form, find the value of each ratio, then write < or > between them' - five requested responses, one compare entry

root_causes.description: render_quick_answers._fmt sympifies string expecteds, and sympify('<') raises SympifyError, so the verified relation for problem 8 degrades to the '---' placeholder reserved for manual-only ids.

improvements.title: Declare a manual verify entry for every explain, name-the-error, or draw-it item
improvements.proposed_change: Any problem whose stem asks the student to explain, justify, say why, name the error, describe, decide which student is right, or draw and label a representation must carry a 'manual' entry in verify.json alongside whatever numeric entries it also needs. Add a lint over the \problem stems in the worksheet tex that flags those constructions and fails the build when the matching problem id has no manual entry, so 'N passed, 0 manual' can only be printed by a sheet that genuinely contains no open response.
improvements.regression_test: Add a lint fixture from curr-151 problem 10, whose stem contains 'Draw a tape diagram with one box per share', paired with a verify JSON declaring only an eval entry for that id. The lint must exit non-zero and name the drawn-representation requirement; adding a manual entry must clear it. Today this input builds green with '0 manual'.
improvements.expected_impact: The gate log's manual count becomes a truthful statement about the sheet, and the prompt's standing instruction to clearly label any genuinely open response for manual review is satisfied structurally instead of by author discretion.
improvements.risk: Verb matching will over-trigger on rhetorical asides such as 'show your thinking' in the directions block. Scope the scan to \problem stems and allow an explicit per-problem acknowledgement flag to suppress a false positive.

improvements.title: Verify every response the worksheet prints a slot for, not only the final numeric result
improvements.proposed_change: Require one verify-JSON entry (machine or manual) per distinct response the sheet asks the student to write, not one per problem id. That covers each lettered sub-part, the remainder half of a 'quotient with a remainder' answer, the person or option a stem asks the learner to name, and every intermediate form a stem explicitly requests before the final one. Enforce it with a gate that counts printed answer locations per problem in the worksheet tex (\ansline, \ansblank, \answerline, and (a)/(b)/(c) part markers inside a \problem stem) and fails the build when a problem's combined machine plus manual entries cover fewer slots than the sheet prints.
improvements.regression_test: Extend the slot gate fixture with curr-151 problem 1: a stem requesting a ratio 'in all three forms' plus a simplest-form fraction, backed by one eval entry. The gate must report uncovered responses until the requested intermediate forms are declared or the stem is narrowed to one response.
improvements.expected_impact: Every printed blank has a checked value behind it, so neither the Quick Answers bank nor a boxed key answer can be a partial answer to the question actually asked.
improvements.risk: Counting slots from tex is heuristic and a stem that prints '(a)' as ordinary prose could raise a false failure. Scope the counter to part markers at the start of a sentence and allow an explicit per-problem slot-count override in the verify JSON.

improvements.title: Stop pushing relation symbols and interval keywords through sympify in the Quick Answers bank
improvements.proposed_change: render_quick_answers._fmt calls sympy.sympify on every string 'expected' and renders whatever comes back. Two vocabularies are not expressions and must be handled before that call. First, relation strings ('<', '>', '=', '<=', '>=') from compare problems raise SympifyError and degrade to the '---' the module documents as meaning 'manual, see solution', so a verified answer is advertised as unavailable. Second, the endpoint and closure triple of an inequality problem contains the literal 'open', which sympify resolves to the Python builtin open() and sympy.latex renders as \mathtt{\text{<built-in function open>}}. Render relations verbatim as math, render an inequality triple as the solution the student writes (x < -3) or as standard interval notation, never sympify the literals open/closed/oo/-oo, and make a sympify result that is not a SymPy object a hard error rather than a rendered repr.
improvements.regression_test: Assert in tests/test_render_quick_answers.py that a relation-type compare entry expecting '<' renders '$<$' rather than '---'. Fails on today's _fmt, passes once relations bypass sympify.
improvements.expected_impact: The at-a-glance grading bank stops printing Python internals into a teacher-facing PDF and stops blanking out every comparison answer on comparison-heavy sheets, where today it can be more than half empty.
improvements.risk: Low. The change is confined to one formatting helper, and the fixture-locked invariant that bank entries stay plain text outside \ans and \boxed is untouched.

case_summary: A strong concept-models ratio packet: thirteen machine checks across ten problems all correct, genuinely varied models (sticker strip, tape diagram, three ratio tables), and the three written forms tied to the models rather than asserted. The gap is the verification contract. Four problems ask the student to explain a choice or draw a diagram and none is declared manual, so a sheet with substantial open response reports '0 manual'; problems 1 and 8 each request several intermediate forms and only the final one is checked. Presentation is otherwise clean apart from problem 8's comparison answer rendering as an em dash in the Quick Answers bank.
